correctness.rationale: Adding one in base b verifies the trailing-(b−1) interpretation of ν_b(n+1), including n=0 and composite b. The declared automaton advances on b−1 and resets on any smaller digit; its lasso starts with a transient positions and ends with a p-cycle. Its initial state is fixed by zero. All states are reached by a suitable string of maximal digits; two states merge only if their entire controller tails agree, since a suffix of t maximal digits tests the t-th entry of the tail. If i<j<a+p and the tails coincide, d=j−i is a period from i onward. Every eventual period of the p-periodic primitive tail is divisible by p (translation by d on residues modulo p would otherwise give period gcd(p,d)). For i≥a this contradicts 0<d<p. For i<a, transfer the p-period identity to every index from i by adding sufficiently many multiples of d to both terms; this contradicts minimal onset a. Thus there are exactly a+p states. With the input-alphabet prefix metric, a word's best state relabeling matches until the first arrival at a state by a different digit than an earlier arrival. Thus earliest conflict at the ℓ-th edge gives raw opacity 2^(1−ℓ), normalized by M_b=1/2, as in Allouche–Yao Theorems 1–2 (no conflict gives zero). For b≥3, 01 is a length-two conflict at the common reset state. For binary a>0 the reset destination is distinct from every advance destination and there is no conflict. For binary a=0 only state 0 can conflict; a one-arrival requires at least p ones since the previous reset or start. If a zero-arrival precedes it, at least p+1 edges are needed, and if the one-arrival comes first, at least one subsequent edge is still needed. 01^p realizes the bound including p=1. A period-p single 1 per period, a constant controller, and a nonperiodic initial entry followed by a constant tail realize all published levels as stated. For arbitrary Y the reviewed invariant is the input-prefix opacity of the intrinsic transition graph as explicitly scoped in RESULT.md line 18; no distance between Y-valued outputs and input digits is asserted. This proof is valid for the whole declared domain. The supplied finite checker and its counts were inspected as recorded evidence, not executed.

value.rationale: Valuation-controlled sequences extend familiar automatic words such as period-doubling. The exact minimization and opacity together explain how one transient segment can make a binary automaton transparent despite the same eventual period, whereas adding a second reset digit makes graph opacity maximal. The full infinite dyadic binary spectrum follows for even just binary-valued controllers. This is useful structural classification beyond any individual known example, within the input-prefix metric only.
